about.title: Susanville Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision changes everything, and it often happens without warning on roads many Susanville residents drive every day, including Main Street, Paul Bunyan Road, and Skyline Road. Lassen County's most recent full-year public records show 14 injury collisions and 18 people injured, with reported crashes tending to cluster on Tuesday afternoons between 2 and 4 p.m. While that same reporting year recorded zero traffic deaths, families across the county have faced this loss before and will again, and they deserve support when it happens. California law allows a spouse, domestic partner, or children to bring a wrongful death claim, with other dependents sometimes eligible depending on the situation. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and we can put you in touch with an independent attorney who takes wrongful death cases on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless money is recovered for your family.

whyChoose.title: Why Families in Susanville Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: We Understand the Standing Rules
items.desc: California limits who can file a wrongful death claim, usually starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children before extending to other dependents. An attorney can help sort out who in your family qualifies to bring the claim.

items.title: Deadlines Move Fast
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks significantly if a government entity was involved. Getting connected early helps preserve evidence and protect your family's options.

items.title: No Cost Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: Independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, so your family pays nothing upfront and owes a fee only if compensation is recovered. That structure lets you focus on grieving instead of legal bills.

items.question: Who in my family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a surviving spouse, registered domestic partner, and children. If none of those exist, certain other dependents or heirs may have standing depending on their relationship to the person who died. An attorney can review your family's situation and clarify who is eligible.

items.question: Susanville's crash data shows zero traffic deaths in the most recent year, so is a wrongful death claim still relevant here?
items.answer: Public crash counts can vary year to year, and a single reporting period doesn't reflect every incident a family in Lassen County may face. Wrongful death claims can arise from crashes on roads like Rt 36 or Skyline Road in any year, and the legal process is the same regardless of how recent county-wide numbers look. If your family has lost someone, the two-year filing deadline still applies.

items.question: What can my family recover through a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: California allows recovery for things like funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their companionship, love, and guidance. Every family's losses look different, and an attorney can walk you through what applies to your circumstances. This is a civil claim, separate from any criminal case tied to the crash.
